method_card.title: Punnett Squares and Genetic Probability
steps: Write each parent's two alleles, then list the gametes each can pass.
Draw a 2 by 2 grid: one parent's gametes across the top, the other's down the side.
Fill the four boxes by combining the row and column alleles.
Count the genotypes or phenotypes, then give a ratio, fraction, or percentage.
method_card.content:
A Punnett square shows the four equally likely allele combinations a child can inherit. A capital letter is a dominant allele (shown if present); a lowercase letter is recessive (shown only as two copies, like bb).

Homozygous means two identical alleles (BB or bb); heterozygous means two different (Bb), also called a carrier when the recessive allele causes a disorder. Bb and bB are the same genotype, so count them together. Read carefully whether the question wants a ratio, a fraction, or a percentage.

exam_context.frequency: Very common: Punnett squares appear on nearly every Paper 2

bronze.display: In a cross between two heterozygous parents (Bb × Bb), what ratio of offspring genotypes would you expect?
bronze.hint: Build the 2 by 2 grid for Bb by Bb, then count how many BB, Bb and bb you get.

misconceptions.message: Bb × Bb gives BB, Bb, Bb, bb, which is 1 BB : 2 Bb : 1 bb.

guided_steps.say: Each parent is Bb, so each can pass B or b. Fill the 2 by 2 grid: BB, Bb, Bb, bb.

guided_steps.hint: Only the top-left box takes B from both parents.

guided_steps.pre: How many boxes are Bb (count Bb and bB together)?
guided_steps.hint: Two boxes mix one B with one b.

guided_steps.say: So far 1 BB and 2 Bb. One box is left.

guided_steps.hint: The bottom-right box takes b from both parents.

guided_steps.done: That gives 1 BB : 2 Bb : 1 bb, which is the first option.
guided_steps.hint: Add the three counts.

bronze.display: Tall pea plants (T) are dominant to short (t). If two heterozygous plants (Tt × Tt) are crossed, what fraction of offspring would you expect to be short?
bronze.hint: Only tt gives the short plant. Count how many of the four boxes are tt.

misconceptions.message: Tt × Tt gives TT, Tt, Tt, tt. Only tt is short = 1 out of 4 = 1/4.

bronze.display: What is the genotype of an organism that is homozygous dominant for a trait represented by the letter A?
bronze.hint: Homozygous means two identical alleles; dominant means capital letters.

misconceptions.message: Homozygous = two identical alleles. Dominant = capital letter. So homozygous dominant = AA.

bronze.display: A homozygous dominant parent (BB) is crossed with a homozygous recessive parent (bb). What percentage of offspring will be heterozygous (Bb)?
bronze.hint: One parent gives only B, the other gives only b, so every box is Bb.

misconceptions.message: If you answered 50, remember every box mixes B from BB with b from bb, so all four are Bb: 100%.

guided_steps.say: BB can only pass B. bb can only pass b. So every box mixes one B with one b.

guided_steps.pre: How many of the four boxes are Bb?
guided_steps.hint: Every box gets B from one parent and b from the other.

guided_steps.pre: How many boxes are BB or bb (homozygous)?
guided_steps.hint: Neither parent can give a matching pair.
All four boxes count.

guided_steps.pre: Check they total four: Bb (4) + others (0) =
guided_steps.done: All four offspring are Bb, so 100% heterozygous is right.
guided_steps.hint: Add the two counts.

bronze.display: In a Bb × Bb cross, how many out of 4 offspring would you expect to show the dominant phenotype?
bronze.hint: Any box with at least one capital B shows the dominant phenotype.

misconceptions.message: If you answered 1, that is the recessive count. BB, Bb and Bb all show the dominant phenotype, so it is 3.

guided_steps.say: Bb × Bb gives BB, Bb, Bb, bb. Any box with at least one B shows the dominant phenotype.

guided_steps.pre: How many boxes contain at least one B?
guided_steps.hint: BB, Bb and Bb all have a capital B.
Only the bb box shows the recessive phenotype.
Take the one recessive box away from four.

guided_steps.done: All four boxes accounted for, so 3 show the dominant phenotype.
guided_steps.hint: Add the two counts.

bronze.display: A parent with genotype Bb produces gametes. Which alleles can be in the gametes?
bronze.hint: A gamete carries just one allele from the pair, not both.

misconceptions.message: Each gamete gets one allele from each pair. A Bb parent makes gametes with either B or b, never both.

bronze.display: Two homozygous recessive parents (bb × bb) are crossed. How many out of 4 offspring will show the recessive phenotype?
bronze.hint: Both parents can only pass b, so work out how many boxes are bb.

misconceptions.message: If you answered 1, you assumed a 3:1 cross. Here BOTH parents are bb, so every box is bb: all 4 show the recessive phenotype.

guided_steps.say: Each parent is bb, so each parent can only pass a b allele.

guided_steps.pre: How many different alleles can a bb parent pass?
guided_steps.hint: Both of its alleles are b.

guided_steps.pre: So how many of the four boxes contain a capital B?
guided_steps.hint: Neither parent has a B to give.
Every box is bb.

guided_steps.done: Every offspring is bb, so all 4 show the recessive phenotype.
guided_steps.hint: Add the two counts.

bronze.display: A Bb × Bb cross produces four offspring. What percentage of the offspring would you expect to be homozygous (either BB or bb)?
bronze.hint: Homozygous means BB or bb. Count both, not just one.

misconceptions.message: If you answered 25, you counted only BB. Homozygous also includes bb, so BB + bb = 2 out of 4 = 50%.
Homozygous means two identical alleles, so both BB and bb count. 1 BB + 1 bb = 2 out of 4 = 50%.

guided_steps.say: Bb × Bb gives BB, Bb, Bb, bb. Homozygous means two identical letters, so BB and bb both count.

guided_steps.hint: Only the top-left box is BB.
Only the bottom-right box is bb.
Add the BB and bb counts.

guided_steps.done: 2 of the 4 boxes are homozygous, so 50% is right.
guided_steps.hint: Divide by four, then times 100.

silver.display: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a recessive allele (f). Two parents who are both carriers (Ff) have a child. What is the percentage chance that the child is a carrier but does NOT have cystic fibrosis?
silver.hint: Carriers are Ff. Do not count the affected ff or the unaffected FF.

misconceptions.message: If you answered 75, you counted ff as well. A carrier is Ff only: 2 out of 4 = 50%.

guided_steps.say: Ff × Ff gives FF, Ff, Ff, ff. A carrier is Ff: two different alleles, but no disease.

guided_steps.hint: Two boxes mix one F with one f.
Only the ff box has the condition.
Divide by four, then times 100.

guided_steps.done: 2 of 4 are carriers, so 50% is right.
guided_steps.hint: Add the three counts.

silver.display: In a cross Bb × bb, how many out of 4 offspring would you expect to show the recessive phenotype?
silver.hint: Cross Bb with bb, then count how many boxes are bb.

misconceptions.message: If you answered 1, you used a Bb × Bb ratio. Bb × bb gives Bb, Bb, bb, bb, so 2 boxes are recessive.

guided_steps.say: Bb passes B or b. bb passes only b. So the grid is Bb, Bb, bb, bb.

guided_steps.hint: Two boxes take the B from the Bb parent.
Two boxes take the b from the Bb parent.
The bb boxes show the recessive phenotype.

guided_steps.done: 2 of 4 are recessive, so the answer is 2.
guided_steps.hint: Add the two counts.

silver.display: Polydactyly is caused by a dominant allele (D). A father with polydactyly (Dd) and an unaffected mother (dd) have children. What is the probability of a child having polydactyly?
silver.hint: Cross Dd with dd and count how many boxes carry a D.

misconceptions.message: Dd × dd gives Dd, Dd, dd, dd. Two have polydactyly (Dd) = 2 out of 4 = 50% = 1 in 2.

silver.display: If 200 offspring are produced from a Bb × Bb cross, how many would you expect to show the DOMINANT phenotype?
silver.hint: Three out of four boxes show the dominant phenotype; scale that up to 200.

misconceptions.message: If you answered 50, that is the recessive quarter. The dominant phenotype is 3 out of 4, so 3/4 of 200 = 150.

guided_steps.say: Bb × Bb gives BB, Bb, Bb, bb. Three of the four boxes show the dominant phenotype.

guided_steps.pre: How many of the four boxes show the dominant phenotype?
guided_steps.hint: Any box with at least one B.
Split 200 equally between the four boxes.
Three boxes, 50 each.
Add the dominant and recessive totals.

silver.display: Tongue rolling (R) is dominant to non-rolling (r). A roller (Rr) and a non-roller (rr) have 80 children. How many would you expect to be non-rollers?
silver.hint: Half the boxes are non-rollers (rr); find half of 80.

misconceptions.message: If you answered 20, you used 1/4. Rr × rr gives Rr, Rr, rr, rr, so HALF are non-rollers: 1/2 of 80 = 40.

guided_steps.say: Rr passes R or r. rr passes only r. The grid is Rr, Rr, rr, rr.

guided_steps.pre: How many of the four boxes are non-rollers (rr)?
guided_steps.hint: Two boxes take the r from the Rr parent.
Split 80 equally between the four boxes.
Two non-roller boxes, 20 each.
Add rollers and non-rollers.

silver.display: Sickle cell trait is caused by allele S. A carrier (AS) and an unaffected person (AA) have 20 children. How many would you expect to be carriers (AS)?
silver.hint: Half the children are carriers; find half of 20.

misconceptions.message: If you answered 5, you used 1/4. AS × AA gives AA, AA, AS, AS, so HALF are carriers: 1/2 of 20 = 10.

guided_steps.say: The carrier AS passes A or S. The unaffected AA passes only A. The grid is AA, AA, AS, AS.

guided_steps.pre: How many of the four boxes are carriers (AS)?
guided_steps.hint: Two boxes take the S from the AS parent.
Split 20 equally between the four boxes.
Two carrier boxes, 5 each.
Add carriers and non-carriers.

gold.display: A couple both have dimples (dominant trait, D). They have a child without dimples. What are the genotypes of both parents?
gold.hint: The no-dimples child must be dd, so each parent had a d to give while still showing dimples.

misconceptions.message: The child without dimples is dd, so inherited a d from each parent. Both parents show dimples, so each also has a D. Both must be Dd.
DD × DD can only give DD. DD × Dd cannot give dd. Only Dd × Dd can produce a dd child.

guided_steps.say: The child has NO dimples. Dimples (D) is dominant, so the no-dimples child must be the double-recessive genotype dd.

guided_steps.pre: How many capital D alleles does a dd child carry?
guided_steps.hint: A recessive trait shows only with two lowercase alleles.

guided_steps.say: So the child inherited one d from EACH parent. But both parents SHOW dimples, so each also carries a D. A parent with one D and one d is written Dd.

guided_steps.pre: How many d alleles must each dimpled parent carry to give a dd child?
guided_steps.hint: The child needs one d from each side.

guided_steps.pre: From Dd × Dd, how many of the four boxes are dd?
guided_steps.hint: Only the box taking d from both parents is dd.

guided_steps.pre: From DD × Dd, how many boxes could be dd?
guided_steps.done: Only Dd × Dd can give a dd child, so both parents are Dd (the third option).
guided_steps.hint: DD has no d to pass, so no box can be dd.

gold.display: Red flower colour (R) is incompletely dominant with white (W). Heterozygous (RW) flowers are pink. If two pink flowers are crossed, what percentage of offspring will be pink?
gold.hint: With incomplete dominance the RW heterozygote is pink; count the RW boxes.

misconceptions.message: If you answered 25, you counted only one box. RW × RW gives RR, RW, RW, WW, so 2 of 4 are pink = 50%.
With incomplete dominance the heterozygote has a blend phenotype. RW × RW gives 1 red : 2 pink : 1 white.

guided_steps.say: RW × RW gives RR (red), RW (pink), RW (pink), WW (white). With incomplete dominance, RW shows as pink.

guided_steps.hint: Two boxes mix one R with one W.
Only the top-left box is RR.
Divide by four, then times 100.

guided_steps.done: 2 of 4 are pink, so 50% is right.
guided_steps.hint: Add the three counts.

gold.display: Colour blindness is sex-linked and recessive, carried on the X chromosome. A carrier mother (Xb on one X) and a father with normal vision have children. What percentage of ALL their children would you expect to have normal colour vision?
gold.hint: Only the affected son (Xb Y) is colour-blind; the other three boxes have normal vision.

misconceptions.message: If you answered 25, that is the colour-blind fraction. Three of the four children have normal vision, so 75%.
The father's Y chromosome carries no allele for this trait. Only the son who gets Xb from his mother is colour-blind.

guided_steps.say: The four children are: a normal-vision daughter, a carrier daughter, a normal-vision son, and a colour-blind son (Xb Y). Only that last son is affected.

guided_steps.pre: How many of the four children are colour-blind?
guided_steps.hint: Only the son who inherits Xb from his mother.

guided_steps.pre: How many have normal colour vision?
guided_steps.hint: Four children minus the one affected son.
Divide by four, then times 100.

guided_steps.done: 3 of 4 children have normal vision, so 75% is right.
guided_steps.hint: Add the two counts.

gold.display: In a genetics experiment, 120 pea plants are produced from a monohybrid cross. 91 have round seeds and 29 have wrinkled seeds. What is the expected ratio, and does the actual data closely fit it?
options: Expected 3:1, and yes: 91:29 is about 3.1:1, which is close
Expected 1:1, and no: the data does not fit
Expected 3:1, but no: 91:29 is too far from 90:30
Expected 1:3, and yes: the data fits well
gold.hint: A 3 to 1 ratio predicts 90 to 30; check how close 91 to 29 is.

misconceptions.message: A 3:1 ratio predicts 90 round : 30 wrinkled. Actual is 91:29. 91 ÷ 29 is about 3.1:1, very close to 3:1.
Real data rarely matches predicted ratios exactly. 91:29 is close enough to 3:1 (predicted 90:30) to support the model.

gold.display: A man with blood type A (genotype AO) and a woman with blood type B (genotype BO) have children. What percentage of their children could have blood type O?
gold.hint: Only the OO box gives type O; that is one box out of four.

misconceptions.message: If you answered 0, remember each parent carries a hidden O. AO × BO gives AB, AO, BO, OO, so the OO box is type O: 25%.
A and B are codominant with each other but both are dominant over O. Only OO gives type O blood.

guided_steps.say: The father AO passes A or O. The mother BO passes B or O. The grid is AB, AO, BO, OO.

guided_steps.pre: How many boxes are OO (type O)?
guided_steps.hint: Only the box taking O from both parents.

guided_steps.pre: How many boxes are NOT type O?
guided_steps.hint: AB, AO and BO all carry an A or a B.
Divide by four, then times 100.

guided_steps.done: 1 of 4 is type O, so 25% is right.
guided_steps.hint: Add the two counts.

gold.display: Two parents who are both heterozygous (Ff) for cystic fibrosis already have 3 children, none affected. Out of every 4 children from this cross, how many would you expect to have cystic fibrosis?
gold.hint: Each pregnancy is independent, so the earlier children do not change the odds.

misconceptions.message: If you answered 0, that is the gambler's fallacy. The 3 healthy children do not change the odds: Ff × Ff still expects 1 in 4 affected.
Previous children being unaffected does NOT raise or lower the chance for the next. It stays at 1 in 4.

guided_steps.say: Each pregnancy is independent, so the 3 healthy children already born do not change anything. Ff × Ff gives FF, Ff, Ff, ff.

guided_steps.pre: How many of the four boxes are ff (cystic fibrosis)?
guided_steps.hint: Only the ff box has the condition.

guided_steps.pre: How many are unaffected (FF or Ff)?
guided_steps.hint: Four boxes minus the one ff box.
Only the ff box.

guided_steps.done: 1 in 4, no matter how many healthy children came before.
guided_steps.hint: Add the two counts.

problem_bank.bronze_description: Read a ready-made cross, fill the grid, and count genotypes or phenotypes.
problem_bank.silver_description: Work out the cross yourself, then turn the ratio into a percentage or a real number of offspring.
problem_bank.gold_description: Handle codominance, sex linkage, blood groups, or reason backwards from the offspring.

worked_examples.question: Two heterozygous parents (Bb × Bb) are crossed. Brown fur (B) is dominant to white fur (b). What percentage of offspring would you expect to have white fur?

steps.label: Step 2: Count phenotypes
steps.content:
BB = brown, Bb = brown (dominant), Bb = brown, bb = white

3 brown : 1 white

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: 25% would have white fur (1 out of 4)

worked_examples.question: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a recessive allele (f). Two carrier parents (Ff × Ff) have a child. What is the probability that the child will have cystic fibrosis?

steps.label: Step 2: Identify affected offspring
steps.content: Only ff has cystic fibrosis (homozygous recessive). That is 1 out of 4 boxes.

worked_examples.question: A couple has four children. Three have brown eyes and one has blue eyes. Blue eyes are recessive (bb). Determine the genotypes of both parents. Explain your reasoning.

steps.label: Step 1: Work backwards from the offspring
steps.content: One child has blue eyes (bb). This means the child must have inherited one b from each parent.

steps.label: Step 2: Determine parent genotypes
steps.content: Both parents must carry at least one b allele. Since both parents have brown eyes (dominant phenotype), they must each also carry one B allele.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Both parents are Bb (heterozygous). This gives a 3:1 ratio, matching 3 brown : 1 blue.

bronze.title: Bronze: read the cross and count
steps: You are given both parents' genotypes. Write the gametes each can pass (one allele each), then draw a 2 by 2 grid.
Fill the four boxes by combining the top allele with the side allele. Bb and bB are the same, so count them together.
Count the genotype or phenotype the question asks for. The recessive phenotype (lowercase pair, like bb) shows only when both alleles are recessive.

example.question: Brown fur (B) is dominant to white (b). Cross Bb × Bb. What fraction is white?

steps.label: Grid
steps.content: Bb × Bb gives BB, Bb, Bb, bb.

steps.label: Count
steps.content: Only bb is white: 1 out of 4 boxes.

silver.title: Silver: turn the ratio into a number
steps: Work out the cross yourself, then find the fraction with the phenotype you want (for example 1/4 recessive, or 1/2 in a cross with one recessive parent).
To scale to a real population, split the total equally between the four boxes: each box is total ÷ 4.
Multiply that share by how many boxes match. Always check your groups add back to the total.

example.question: Tt × Tt gives 40 plants. How many are short (tt)?

gold.title: Gold: special inheritance and reverse clues
steps: Some crosses are not simple dominant and recessive. In codominance and incomplete dominance the heterozygote has its own phenotype (roan, pink), so count it separately.
Sex-linked alleles sit on the X chromosome; a son has only one X, so one recessive X allele already shows.
To work backwards, use a recessive child (double-recessive genotype) to pin down what alleles each parent must carry.

example.question: Red (R) and white (W) coat alleles are codominant; RW is roan. Cross RR × RW. What fraction is roan?

steps.label: Grid
steps.content: RR × RW gives RR, RR, RW, RW.

steps.say: Each parent carries two alleles, one B and one b, like two tokens in a bag. Each parent passes ONE token to the child, at random. The grid shows every equally likely pair the child could end up with.
steps.pre: How many equally likely combinations are in the grid?

steps.say: A recessive trait, say blue eyes, only appears when the child gets TWO b tokens, bb.
steps.pre: How many of the four boxes are bb?
steps.hint: Only the bottom-right box has b and b.

steps.say: So 1 out of 4, a quarter, 25%. That grid IS a Punnett square, and the cross is written Bb × Bb. Filling boxes and counting them is the whole skill.

steps.say: The grid is BB, Bb, Bb, bb. White fur needs two recessive alleles, bb.

steps.pre: How many boxes are brown (have a B)?
steps.hint: BB, Bb and Bb all have a capital B.

steps.done: 1 of 4 is white, so 25%. That is the whole bronze move: read the grid and count.

steps.say: The grid is RR, Rr, Rr, rr. Non-rollers need two recessive alleles, rr.

steps.pre: How many of the four boxes are non-rollers (rr)?

A red bull (RR) is crossed with a roan cow (RW). What percentage of calves are roan?

steps.say: The bull RR passes only R. The cow RW passes R or W. The grid is RR, RR, RW, RW. Because the alleles are codominant, RW shows as roan, not red.

steps.hint: Two boxes take the W from the cow.
Two boxes take the R from the cow.

steps.done: 2 of 4 are roan, so 50%. The gold move is spotting that the heterozygote has its own phenotype.
